newsitem.title: INDIA: India 96/97 industrial output seen rising 10 pct.
newsitem.headline: India 96/97 industrial output seen rising 10 pct.

text.p: India's index of industrial production is expected to rise by about 10 percent in 1996/97 (April-March) over the previous fiscal year, Industry Ministry Secretary T.R. Prasad said on Wednesday.

Prasad, who works in the ministry's department of industrial policy and promotion, told a conference on competitiveness in the Indian capital that the index rose by about 9.8 percent over the first six months of the 1996/97 fiscal year.
"The next six months have shown a moderate decline," said Prasad, who is chairman of the Foreign Investment Promotion Board.

Prasad said some sectors are under-performing, citing domestic crude oil, fertilisers and consumer durables. But he said the capital goods industry, which he called the backbone of Indian industry, is doing very well, as are automobiles.
Prasad said the industrial production index was a lagging indicator and would later be revised. "One need not really worry in the short-term context," he said.
"If you ask me to bet on a number, I'd bet on 10 percent," he said, referring to estimated 1996/97 industrial growth.
"Even if we miss it, we'll come within shooting distance of the number 10," he said.
The industrial production index rose by 9.8 percent between April and October 1996, compared with the same seven-month period in 1995, according to official figures.
